sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: hook h10, a precision the documents do not print over a printed tie (Hard shape A): both banks print the regulatory CET1 ratio to one decimal, and the printed declines are identical (20 basis points); the components each prints beside them give 23.76 and 18.12. Target hard. Sentence and answer carried word for word from sketch i06 (origin claude, 2026-10-18). Local strong-solver screen on this exact sentence: 3/3 right, high confidence (one solver medium on which reading is intended) (record in notes/sketches/i06.md; raw returns runs/i06-screen-2cfcfa4976a8bfe0/returns/; ledger row 81). User quick test against the High model, 2026-10-18: survived ("i06 survived"); a quick test sets no tier. Platform difficulty result pending. Doc numbers: D05 = Doc 3 (KeyCorp release and supplement), D04 = Doc 5 (Huntington supplement); D03 = Doc 4 (Huntington release) is not used.
- Dependency plan: Doc 3 CET1 17,038 / 17,016 and risk-weighted assets 149,338 / 152,317 (March 31 / June 30) -> 11.40902% and 11.17144%, fall 0.23758 points; Doc 5 CET1 21,160 / 21,388 and risk-weighted assets 208,132 / 214,192 -> 10.16663% and 9.98543%, fall 0.18119 points; difference 0.05639 points = 5.639 basis points -> 6.
- Universe: not applicable (one derived difference).
- Necessity: D05 (Doc 3) is the only KeyCorp document; its CET1 capital and risk-weighted assets appear only in the reconciliation table (L783, L791). D04 (Doc 5) is the only source of Huntington's CET1 capital in dollars (L996, L1015); D03 prints the ratios (10.0, 10.2) and risk-weighted assets in $ billions only (L403), so it cannot give basis-point precision. Delete-and-guess: without D04, a solver has one-decimal ratios only and answers 0 (or cannot answer); without D05, KeyCorp's change is unknown. D01 and D02 (Fifth Third) carry no KeyCorp or Huntington figures.
- Selected-lever checks: Ask for a precision the document doesn't print: the printed ratios give 11.4 - 11.2 = 0.2 and 10.2 - 10.0 = 0.2, a difference of 0 (D05 L61 also prints the change as "(20)"); rejected by "to the nearest basis point", since one-decimal ratios cannot resolve basis points and both banks print the components. Look-alike metric: the AOCI-inclusive ratios (KeyCorp "Marked CET1" 14,886 / 149,338 -> 14,862 / 152,317, a 21.07 fall; Huntington "Adjusted CET1" 19,154 / 208,132 -> 19,347 / 214,192, a 17.03 fall) give 4.04 -> 4; rejected because the question names the regulatory ratio, whose rows carry that name, while the look-alikes are named "Marked CET1" and "Adjusted CET1".
- Targeted failure modes: declared Document convention / Rounding, scale or sign -> 0 (Doc 3 L216 and L61, Doc 5 L235 and L1007: one-decimal ratios, both 20 basis points), recomputed in scratchpad calc_aq06809.py. Not declared: the AOCI-inclusive look-alike (4), which no screen solver took (all three named it as weak), per the rule to declare only the lazy-default wrong answer.
- Calculation verification: Python fractions (scratchpad calc_aq06809.py, 2026-10-18): KeyCorp 11.409018% -> 11.171438% (fall 0.2375800 points), Huntington 10.166625% -> 9.985434% (fall 0.1811914), difference 0.0563886 points = 5.6389 basis points -> 6. Each computed ratio rounds to the printed one-decimal ratio in every column (screen solvers checked June 2025 and December 2025 as well). Inputs are whole millions; a half-million shift moves a ratio by under 0.0004 points, so the result cannot leave the 5.5-6.5 band. Rounding each fall to whole basis points first (24 - 18) also gives 6.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: "common equity tier 1" and "CET1" across all five texts: KeyCorp ratio rows D05 L20, L61, L216, L608, L793 (all one decimal); capital rows only L783 (and the marked line L787); Huntington ratio rows D03 L45, L94, L400, D04 L235, L1007, L1021 (all one decimal); capital rows D04 L996, L1015. No document prints either ratio to two decimals or the declines in basis points beyond KeyCorp's "(20)".
- Precision/readings: (a) printed ratios -> 0 (main alternative; all three screen solvers named it and rejected it on "nearest basis point"). (b) AOCI-inclusive ratios -> 4. (c) Relative declines (2.08% vs 1.78%, a 0.30-point gap read as 30 "basis points") -> 30, a stretched reading one solver noted. (d) Huntington's risk-weighted assets taken from D03's $ billions (214.2 / 208.1) -> 5.45 -> 5; D04 prints the millions on the line beside the capital it needs. June 30, 2026 figures are estimates in both tables, used as printed.
- Completeness: capture complete (5 of 5 documents, no gap characters); both capital tables read in full.
- Style/set review: one ask, 31 words. Only question in the bundle so far; earlier sketches i01-i05, i07 were closed after quick tests or a wording defect; no shared answer path with them (i06 is the only capital sketch).

sections.question: What was the difference, in basis points to the nearest basis point, between the declines in KeyCorp's and Huntington's common equity tier 1 ratios from March 31 to June 30, 2026?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliations, capital rows): KeyCorp's common equity tier 1 capital was $17,038 million at March 31, 2026 and $17,016 million at June 30, 2026, against risk-weighted assets of $149,338 million and $152,317 million. Doc 3 computes the ratio as this capital over risk-weighted assets and prints it to one decimal, 11.4% and 11.2%.
Step 2. Calculation (Doc 3): fall in KeyCorp's ratio from March 31 to June 30: 17,038 / 149,338 - 17,016 / 152,317 = 0.23758%.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, Basel III capital table): Huntington's common equity tier 1 capital was $21,160 million at March 31, 2026 and $21,388 million at June 30, 2026, against risk-weighted assets of $208,132 million and $214,192 million. Doc 5 computes its ratio the same way and prints it to one decimal, 10.2% and 10.0%.
Step 4. Calculation (Doc 5): fall in Huntington's ratio over the same dates: 21,160 / 208,132 - 21,388 / 214,192 = 0.18119%.
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 3 and Doc 5): KeyCorp's fall less Huntington's, from the unrounded ratios: 17,038 / 149,338 - 17,016 / 152,317 - 21,160 / 208,132 + 21,388 / 214,192 = 0.05639%.
Step 6. Final answer (Doc 3 and Doc 5): in basis points, 0.05639% × 10,000 = 5.639, which rounds to 6.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Document convention
How a careless solver fails: Rounding, scale or sign

Why these are traps: Doc 3 prints KeyCorp's CET1 ratio as 11.4% then 11.2% and Doc 5 prints Huntington's as 10.2% then 10.0%: both fall 20 basis points, so a careless solver answers 0. Capital over risk-weighted assets gives falls of 23.76 and 18.12 basis points, a difference of 6.
